classes.name: Quittio\Core\Builder\InvoiceBuilder
classes.summary: Fluent builder for InvoiceData.
classes.description:
Amounts, prices and quantities are passed as strings or integers, never as floats.
The result is not yet calculated; totals and the VAT breakdown are set by the calculator.

methods.name: from
methods.summary: Starts a builder from existing data, e.g. to change a draft.
methods.description:
For data with a declared VAT total in accounting currency (BT-111) but without exchange
rate (e.g. read from XML) the implied rate is taken over, so that BT-111 is recalculated.
Once lines, allowances, charges or the VAT accounting currency (BT-6) change, the implied
rate is dropped: it is only as precise as the declared amounts and holds only for the
declared currency, so set the rate with exchangeRate() (BR-53 otherwise).
Percentage document allowances and charges on the line sum of their VAT group, and
discounts split over the VAT groups (discountAmount(), discountPercent()), follow the
lines when lines are added, changed or removed.

As long as nothing amount-relevant changes, declared line net amounts and the VAT breakdown
that the recalculation does not reproduce (e.g. rounded per line by another system) are kept
by the calculator (Meta::FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS with a fingerprint of the amount inputs).
Data flagged earlier whose amount inputs no longer match its fingerprint (e.g. changed with
with() or in stored JSON) is treated as changed lines and recalculated.

methods.name: taxCurrency
methods.summary: VAT accounting currency (BT-6). With an exchange rate, BT-111 is calculated.

methods.name: buyerReference
methods.summary: Buyer reference (BT-10). For public sector buyers in Germany this is the Leitweg-ID.

methods.name: seller
methods.summary: The seller (BG-4).
methods.description:
A SellerParty, a PartyBuilder (Party::make()) or an application model (ProvidesParty)
replaces the seller set before. If the builder was started with the defaults of a seller
(applyDefaults(), e.g. Quittio::invoice() with the seller of config/quittio.php or the
current Managed issuer), another seller gets nothing of them: everything they set is
removed again, i.e. the bank account and the small business flag, for a Managed issuer
also payment terms, presentation, locale, time zone and currency. Values the caller set
on the builder stay, also when they were set before seller().

A callable receives the builder of the seller set before and changes it, e.g.
->seller(fn ($s) => $s->contact('Max Muster')); the seller stays the same, and so do its
defaults.

methods.name: buyer
methods.summary: The buyer (BG-7): a BuyerParty, a PartyBuilder (Party::make()) or an application model (ProvidesParty), e.g. ->buyer($customer), replace the buyer set before; a callable receives the builder of the buyer set before and changes it.

methods.name: payee

throws.description: for identifiers or schemes next to a PayeeParty or a callable

methods.summary: Payee (BG-10), if different from the seller (e.g. a factoring company): the name with the identifier (BT-60) and the legal registration identifier (BT-61) and their schemes, a PartyBuilder (Party::make('Factoring AG')->identifier(…)), a PayeeParty, or a callable that receives a PartyBuilder and, like seller() and buyer(), continues an earlier payee.

methods.name: deliveryDate
methods.summary: Actual delivery or service date (BT-72).

methods.name: deliverTo
methods.summary: Deliver-to party and address (BT-70, BG-15).

methods.name: invoicingPeriod
methods.summary: Invoicing period (BG-14).

methods.name: payment
methods.summary: Payment instructions (BG-16) with an optional credit transfer account (BG-17).
methods.description:
A second call replaces the payment instructions: an account given here replaces the
accounts, and data of other payment means is dropped (e.g. bank accounts when switching
to direct debit). Without an account, existing accounts are kept for credit transfers
(e.g. a seller default account); likewise card (BG-18) and direct debit (BG-19) data for
card payments and direct debits. The remittance information (BT-83) is kept unless a new
one is given. Further accounts are added with creditTransfer().

methods.name: creditTransfer
methods.summary: Adds a further bank account (BG-17).

methods.name: dueInDays
methods.summary: Payment target: the due date (BT-9) is the issue date plus $days unless dueDate() is set, and the payment terms say "Payable within … days without deduction." Continues the payment terms set before.

methods.name: cashDiscount
methods.summary: Cash discount ("Skonto") of $percent for payment within $days days after the issue date, optionally on a base amount; repeatable for several tiers. Continues the payment terms.

methods.name: lateFee
methods.summary: Late payment terms: days, percentage and text. Continues the payment terms.

methods.name: paymentTerms
methods.summary: Payment terms (BT-20): a PaymentTerms object or a text replace earlier terms; a callable receives a PaymentTermsBuilder that continues the earlier terms, also those of a PaymentTerms object or of from(), like seller() and buyer().

methods.name: allowance
methods.summary: Document level allowance (BG-20) for one VAT category and rate.
methods.description:
The exemption reason (BT-120/BT-121) is used for the VAT breakdown when no invoice
line of the same VAT group provides one, e.g. an exempt charge on a standard rated invoice.

methods.name: charge
methods.summary: Document level charge (BG-21) for one VAT category and rate. See allowance() for the exemption reason.

methods.name: discountPercent
methods.summary: Percentage discount on all lines. Split into one allowance per VAT group.

methods.name: discountAmount
methods.summary: Absolute discount distributed over all VAT groups in proportion to their line totals.

methods.name: attachment
methods.summary: Supporting document (BG-24), either embedded ($content) or as external link.

methods.name: line
methods.summary: Adds a line (BG-25): a name with the common values (->line('Consulting', netPrice: '120.00', quantity: 4, unit: UnitCode::Hour)), a LineBuilder (Line::make()), an array with the keys of LineBuilder::ARRAY_KEYS, an application model (ProvidesInvoiceLine), a callable that receives a new LineBuilder, or a finished InvoiceLine.

methods.name: updateLine
methods.summary: Changes an existing line, e.g. of a correction draft started with {@see self::from()}: with the named values ->updateLine('2', netPrice: '80.00', quantity: 3), or with a callable that receives the InvoiceLine and returns the changed one, e.g. ->updateLine('2', fn (InvoiceLine $l) => $l->with(['note' => 'Delivered in two parts'])). methods.name: prepaid

methods.name: addPrepaid
methods.summary: Adds to the amount already paid (BT-113), e.g. one of several advance payments.

methods.name: rounding
methods.summary: Rounding amount (BT-114), e.g. cash rounding. Never use it to fix wrong totals.

methods.name: presentation
methods.summary: Design of this invoice in PDF and HTML: a Presentation replaces it, an array changes single values (->presentation(['introText' => 'Thank you for your order.', 'showGrossPrices' => true])), a callable receives the current Presentation and returns the new one.

methods.name: group
methods.summary: Defines a line group for the PDF. Lines join it via LineBuilder::group().

methods.name: flag
methods.summary: Sets a flag that country packs evaluate (e.g. a small amount invoice in Germany).

methods.name: applyDefaults
methods.summary: Applies the defaults of a seller, e.g. the seller of config/quittio.php with its bank account and small business flag (Quittio::invoice()) or a Managed issuer. The builder remembers what they set: seller() with another seller removes it again.

methods.name: defaultVat
methods.summary: VAT treatment of the lines that set none (also sub lines), with the arguments of LineBuilder::vat(). Without it, the application default of useDefaultVat() applies.

methods.name: useDefaultVat
methods.summary: Application default VAT of lines that set none, for invoices without defaultVat(): a preset, or a callable that receives the seller's country code and whether the invoice is flagged as small business invoice (Meta::FLAG_SMALL_BUSINESS) and returns a preset or null, e.g. Quittio\Core\Tax\CountryDefaultVat. methods.name: buildDraft
methods.summary: Builds without requiring lines, e.g. for payment reminders or account statements, or for drafts. classes.name: Quittio\Core\Calculation\AllowanceSplitter
classes.summary: Splits a document discount over several VAT groups.
classes.description:
A document allowance has exactly one VAT category and rate. A discount on
all lines is therefore split into one allowance per VAT group, in proportion
to the signed line sum of the group. Rounding differences are distributed with
the largest remainder method, so that the parts add up exactly to the total
discount. A group with a negative sum (returns) receives a negative part.

For percentage discounts, base amount and percentage are kept on a part only
if the part equals round2(base × percent / 100); otherwise only the amount is
written, because validators check that formula (e.g. PEPPOL-EN16931-R040).

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Calculation\DeclaredAmounts
classes.summary: Declared amounts of an existing document (Meta::FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS): whether they are needed at all, and the fingerprint of the amount inputs they belong to.
classes.description:
The fingerprint (Meta::amountsFingerprint(), set by the calculator on every result and by the
builder on data with amounts) covers per line (with sub lines) the identifier, quantity,
prices, base quantity, VAT category and rate, line allowances and charges and the net amount,
the document allowances and charges, the VAT breakdown and the currency. Data whose
fingerprint no longer matches was changed afterwards (e.g. with with() or in stored JSON):
its amounts are stale and never kept. Data without fingerprint (e.g. read from XML) is taken
as declared by its issuer.

constants.name: LINE_TOLERANCE
constants.summary: Tolerance of a declared line net amount (BT-131), as PEPPOL-EN16931-R120 tolerates it.

constants.name: TAX_CURRENCY_TOLERANCE
constants.summary: Tolerance of a declared VAT total in accounting currency (BT-111) against round2(BT-110 × exchange rate): EN 16931 does not check it, the cumulative rounding of partial cancellations (Corrections\CancellationHistory) needs one cent.

methods.name: needed
methods.summary: Whether the recalculation does not reproduce the declared line net amounts (BT-131), the declared VAT breakdown (BT-116, BT-117) or the declared VAT total in accounting currency (BT-111) exactly, e.g. because another system rounded per line or a partial cancellation aligns its VAT with earlier ones. Data calculated by Quittio never needs declared amounts.

methods.name: isTrusted
methods.summary: Data flagged with declared amounts whose amount inputs still match the fingerprint.

methods.name: breakdownKey
methods.summary: VAT group key of a breakdown; categories without rate (O) ignore a rate written as 0.

methods.name: hasAmounts
methods.summary: Whether the data carries line net amounts or a VAT breakdown.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Calculation\En16931Calculator
classes.summary: Calculation according to EN 16931.
classes.description:
Amounts are rounded half up to two decimals at the defined points only.
VAT is calculated per VAT group (category and rate), not per line (BR-CO-17).

With Meta::FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS (cancellations and unchanged data of InvoiceBuilder::from()
whose declared amounts another system rounded differently) and a matching fingerprint of the
amount inputs (DeclaredAmounts), declared line net amounts (BT-131) within 0.02 of quantity ×
price ± allowances and charges (PEPPOL-EN16931-R120) and declared VAT category tax amounts
(BT-117) less than one currency unit from the recalculation (BR-CO-17) are kept; otherwise
the recalculated amounts are used and Meta::FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS_RECALCULATED is set
(QUITTIO-DECLARED-AMOUNTS). Data whose amount inputs changed after the amounts were declared
(fingerprint mismatch, e.g. a change with with() or in stored JSON) is recalculated completely.
A declared VAT total in accounting currency (BT-111, Meta::declaredVatInTaxCurrency()) is kept
within 0.01 of round2(BT-110 × exchange rate), e.g. the BT-111 of a partial cancellation
aligned with the earlier ones (Corrections\CancellationHistory). In gross price mode the rounding amount (BT-114) follows
the amounts finally used, so that the amount due stays the gross amount of the lines.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Calculation\GrossPriceConverter
classes.summary: Gross price mode for B2C and shops.
classes.description:
Shops calculate with prices including VAT, EN 16931 calculates net. Per VAT group:

  1. G = Σ g_i with g_i = round2(quantity × price incl. VAT)
  2. N = round2(G / (1 + rate / 100)); a partial cancellation aligned with the earlier ones
     declares its N (Corrections\CancellationHistory), which is used within 0.01
  3. T = round2(N × rate / 100)              (BR-CO-17)
  4. Every line gets n_i = round2(g_i / (1 + rate / 100)); the few cents N − Σ n_i
     are added to the lines with the largest rounding remainders. Each line keeps the
     sign of its gross amount (returns and vouchers stay negative). Net prices are
     derived with the precision needed so that the line formula yields the line amount.
  5. G − (N + T) is returned as rounding amount for BT-114, so that the amount
     due equals the gross amount the customer saw. The calculator takes BT-114 from
     the total G and the amounts it finally uses, so that it also holds when
     declared amounts are kept (e.g. the aligned VAT of a partial cancellation).

Limits: all lines must use gross prices, and gross lines must not have line or
document allowances or charges. Model shipping costs and discounts as lines; a
discount line needs a negative quantity, because prices must not be negative (BR-27).

methods.name: netOf
methods.summary: N = round2(G / (1 + rate / 100)), step 2.

params.name: nets
params.description: declared net amounts N per VAT group (key: DeclaredAmounts::breakdownKey()), e.g. of a partial cancellation aligned with the earlier ones (Corrections\CancellationHistory); used instead of step 2 within 0.01

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Calculation\LargestRemainder
classes.summary: Distributes an amount over weights so that the rounded parts add up exactly (largest remainder method).
classes.description:
Weights are signed: each part is total × weight / Σ weights, so a negative weight
(e.g. a VAT group that only contains returns) receives a part with the opposite sign.

returns.description: parts with $scale decimals, same keys as $weights

throws.description: if the weights are not all zero but add up to zero

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Calculation\LineCalculator
classes.summary: Calculates the invoice line net amount (BT-131):
classes.description:
net price   BT-146 = BT-148 − BT-147 (if list price and discount are given)
  base amount B      = round2(BT-129 × BT-146 / (BT-149 ?: 1))
  allowance   A_i    = BT-136 or round2((BT-137 ?: B) × BT-138 / 100)
  charge      C_i    = BT-141 or round2((BT-142 ?: B) × BT-143 / 100)
  line amount BT-131 = B − Σ A_i + Σ C_i

methods.name: exactAmount
methods.summary: Unrounded line amount as PEPPOL-EN16931-R120 checks it: quantity × (net price / base quantity) + line charges − line allowances (BT-129, BT-146, BT-149, BT-141, BT-136). Null without net price (BT-146).

methods.name: priceFor
methods.summary: Smallest-precision net price (2 to 10 decimals) for which the line formula yields exactly $amount.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Corrections\Cancellation
classes.summary: Full cancellation of an issued invoice: a new invoice with its own number that reverses the original and refers to it (BG-3).
classes.description:
Sign strategies (17.2):
- credit_note:      type code 381, amounts positive; UBL writes a CreditNote document,
- negative_invoice: type code 380, quantities and allowance/charge amounts negated.

The cancellation of a credit note is an invoice (380) with the same positive amounts in
both strategies.

Self-billed documents stay self-billed (issued by the buyer, labelled "Gutschrift" by the
kept regulatory note): a self-billed invoice (389) or debit note (527) is cancelled by a
self-billed credit note (261) or a negative self-billed invoice (389), a self-billed credit
note by a self-billed invoice (389) with positive amounts.

Both are permitted in Germany; apart from self-billing the document must not be called
"Gutschrift". The original data is never changed.

Declared amounts (Meta::FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS): a full cancellation reverses the declared
line net amounts (BT-131) and the declared VAT breakdown (BT-116, BT-117) of the original,
also if another system rounded differently (BT-131 within 0.02, PEPPOL-EN16931-R120; BT-117
within the tolerance of BR-CO-17), so that the totals BT-106 to BT-115 are reversed exactly.
A partial cancellation keeps the declared amounts of whole cancelled lines; quantities and
amounts of a line are recalculated. Its VAT is that of the cancelled part, round2(taxable
amount × rate) per VAT group, unless a CancellationHistory of the earlier partial
cancellations is given: then the VAT is rounded cumulatively per group and declared
(Meta::FLAG_CANCELLATION_VAT_ALIGNED), so that all cancellations together reverse exactly the
taxable amount (BT-116) and the VAT (BT-117) of every group and BT-111 in accounting currency.
In gross price mode the net amounts follow cumulatively from the gross amounts cancelled so far
(round2(G / (1 + rate)) like the original) and the rounding amount (BT-114) from the amounts used,
so that the amount due stays the gross amount of the cancelled lines. Every cancellation then
differs by at most 0.01 from round2(own taxable amount × rate), with the sign of its taxable
amount (QUITTIO-CANCELLATION-VAT-ALIGNED, mentioned in the cancellation note); for an original
whose VAT another system rounded, from round2(own taxable amount × the original's BT-117 /
BT-116), which spreads that rounding over the parts. A history that does not fit the original
(CancellationHistory::assertFits()) is rejected.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Corrections\CancellationHistory
classes.summary: What the earlier partial cancellations of an invoice cancelled per VAT group (category and rate), so that the VAT of the next partial cancellation is rounded cumulatively.
classes.description:
VAT is rounded per document and VAT group (BR-CO-17). Rounded per partial cancellation on its
own, the cancellations together can differ from the original by a cent per earlier part (e.g.
9.67 + 9.67 + 9.66 net at 19 %: 3 × 1.84 = 5.52 against 5.51). With a history, per group:

  S      = taxable amount of the earlier cancellations + taxable amount of this one
  target = round2(S × rate / 100), half up like the calculator; the original's VAT (BT-117)
           when this cancellation closes the group (all its lines are then cancelled
           completely)
  VAT    = target − VAT of the earlier cancellations

After every cancellation the VAT cancelled so far is that of the taxable amount cancelled so
far, and once all lines are cancelled exactly the original's VAT (1.84, 1.83, 1.84 = 5.51 in the
example). For an original whose VAT another system rounded (BT-117 ≠ round2(BT-116 × rate)),
the target is round2(S × BT-117 / BT-116): its rounding difference is spread over the parts in
proportion to their taxable amounts instead of falling on the part that closes the group.

In gross price mode the taxable amount follows the same way from the gross amount G of the
lines: N = round2(G cancelled so far / (1 + rate / 100)) as for the original
(GrossPriceConverter), the original's BT-116 when the group closes, minus the taxable amount
already cancelled. The taxable amounts of all cancellations then add up exactly to the
original's, and so do the rounding amounts (BT-114).

Every cancellation therefore differs from round2(own taxable amount × rate) (or × the original's
effective rate) by at most 0.01, which BR-CO-17 tolerates, and its VAT keeps the sign of its
taxable amount (0.00 on 0.00); assertFits() rejects a history for which this would not hold. The
VAT total in accounting currency (BT-111) follows the same way: round2(VAT cancelled so far ×
exchange rate), and the original's BT-111 when the cancellation closes all groups.

Amounts are signed in the original's direction: a credit note that cancels an invoice and the
invoice that cancels a credit note count with their amounts, a negative invoice (strategy
negative_invoice) with its amounts negated.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\View\MandatoryFieldGuard
classes.summary: Checks after rendering that the template printed all mandatory values.
classes.description:
A custom template could omit mandatory information (e.g. the VAT identifier); then PDF
and XML would differ in content. Access keys are view model paths:

- "[*]" stands for every index: "vatRows[*].amount" requires the amount of every VAT row;
- "&" combines paths that must all be printed, "|" separates alternatives;
- a path counts only where the view model has a value: paths of null values and empty
  lists are not required, and a field whose alternatives all have no value is skipped.

Only printed leaf values count (see {@see ViewNode}).

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Xml\XmlSecurity
classes.summary: Safe XML loading for untrusted input.
classes.description:
- Documents with a DOCTYPE are rejected (no entity expansion, no XXE).
- No network access (LIBXML_NONET), no entity substitution (no LIBXML_NOENT).
- Size limit for the input.
- Start tags are limited in length and number of attributes: libxml2 before 2.12
  checks attributes for duplicates in quadratic time.
- The number of namespace declarations in scope is limited: libxml2 before 2.12 looks
  up every prefix by a linear search through all declarations in scope.
- Only encodings in which the markup is ASCII (UTF-8, ISO-8859-*, windows-125*) and
  UTF-16 are accepted; UTF-7 or EBCDIC would hide the markup from these checks.
